answer: Sybils stall when admission runs through a slow shared cost curve instead of a flat fee. Each new identity must attest for real peers to gain trust, and that trust travels only along countersigned edges. A gale of fresh accounts starts with zero edges, so they cannot vouch for one another without first grinding through the same unverified backlog. Honest operators deepen their record steadily, like a river fed by steady rain, while every fake head pays that umber of sunk work separately, with no shortcut. Pooling accounts fails: shared countersigns collapse into one detected cluster.
